sweep5.detail: Walked the spec's 21 sections in order, proving each named artefact with a command rather than by reading. Roles & Permission Matrix -> 6 capabilities, lowercase-dashed in packages/validation/src/index.ts and PascalCase in roles.ts, grants matching the matrix row for row (roles.ts:98-150). Functional requirements 1-47 -> validators/parsers in packages/validation/src/requests.ts and services in apps/api/src/requests. API Contracts -> 8 route headings, 11 handlers in requests.controller.ts:39-165, all under @UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard) at :34-35. Data Model -> 3 tables, 6 indexes and 9 FKs, schema.prisma and migration.sql agreeing exactly; the one column added to an existing table is `ALTER TABLE "Organization" ADD COLUMN "nextRequestNumber" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, which is additive and safe for the previous image (CLAUDE.md migration rule). State Machine -> 8 invariants; lockRequest (requests.service.ts:793-808) issues FOR UPDATE and all 5 transaction blocks call it. Error Messages -> 31 rows, every `Export` present in REQUEST_MESSAGES with byte-identical text (scripted compare, 0 missing, 0 mismatched). Required data-testid -> all 42 present under apps/web. Test Cases -> all 41 ids (TC-01-UNIT/INT/E2E) referenced from code, 0 unreferenced. Requirement 47 negative artefact confirmed: no mail import anywhere in apps/api/src/requests. Every section contributed at least one artefact except Out of Scope and Known Gaps, which state non-goals.

findings.claim: `run.headAtInit = git('rev-parse','HEAD')` advances the static gate's spec-immutability baseline over every commit made before the resume, not only over the person's. The gate it moves is the one that stops an implement stage rewriting its own contract, and the code cannot tell the two authors apart. The same commit widens the door: the entry guard changed from `if (!run.halt) fail(...)` to `if (run.status === 'ready') fail(...)` (:557), so a run that was never halted at all - one whose orchestrator merely died - is now resumable, and resuming it launders any spec edit already committed inside it.

witness.detail: An implement attempt commits code plus an edit to specs/requests/01-requests.md, which .claude/agents/implementer.md forbids. ship.mjs starts static_gate; the orchestrator is killed before a verdict is written, leaving run.status='static_gate' and that stage 'running'. A person runs `node scripts/wf.mjs resume --stage static_gate` - permitted by the new abandoned-run path at wf.mjs:557, and refused outright before this commit. wf.mjs:584 sets run.headAtInit to a HEAD that already contains the implementer's spec edit. static-gate.mjs:59 reads `runStart = run?.headAtInit` and :74 runs `git diff --name-only <runStart> -- specs`, which is now empty, so rule 1 `pipeline/spec-immutable` reports nothing. The run proceeds to review and QA measured against a contract the implementation stage rewrote, and the human never sees the finding that exists to tell them.
witness.source: scripts/static-gate.mjs:74-85, which quotes CLAUDE.md:4 - "When behaviour and spec disagree, the spec wins — change the spec first, deliberately" - as rule 1's own witness

findings.suggestedFix: Before advancing the mark, compute `git diff --name-only run.headAtInit HEAD -- specs`. If it is non-empty, refuse the resume until the operator names the files explicitly (a `--accept-spec-edits <paths>` flag, recorded in the `resumes` entry), or record them in `run.acknowledgedSpecEdits` and have static-gate rule 1 report anything not on that list. The gate then keeps asking "did the implementation stage edit its own contract" instead of "has anything changed since a person last touched the run".

findings.claim: The resume guard is there to enforce "handoff.json still describes the spec on disk", but the question it asks is "does the spec hash equal the hash recorded at init". `run.specSha` is written in exactly one place, cmdInit at wf.mjs:405, and cmdResume never re-stamps it. So the moment a run replans against a corrected spec - which is the recovery this very guard's failure message recommends - the run becomes permanently un-resumable past pre_implement, and the refusal it prints is false.

witness.detail: A run halts with a spec-defect finding at review. The person corrects specs/requests/01-requests.md and runs `node scripts/wf.mjs resume --stage pre_implement`; the guard at :566 is skipped because STAGES.indexOf('pre_implement') > STAGES.indexOf('pre_implement') is false. pre_implement recompiles handoff.json from the corrected spec, and run.specSha is left holding the pre-correction hash. The run later halts again - say a contested finding at review - and the person runs `node scripts/wf.mjs resume --stage review`. Now sha !== run.specSha and STAGES.indexOf('review') > STAGES.indexOf('pre_implement'), so :567 fails with "specs/requests/01-requests.md changed since this run was planned, so handoff.json describes a spec that no longer exists ... Start a new run". handoff.json describes exactly the spec on disk. The observable wrong result is that the person is forced into a whole new run and a fresh pre_implement, which is the cost this command exists to avoid.
witness.source: scripts/wf.mjs:405 is the sole writer of run.specSha; scripts/wf.mjs:566-572 is the reader

findings.suggestedFix: When the resume target is `pre_implement` and the sha has moved, re-stamp `run.specSha = sha` and record the previous value in the `resumes` entry, beside the `headAtInit.from/to` the same commit already records. The invariant then reads "specSha is the sha the current plan was built from", which is the question the guard on the later stages is trying to ask.

The Summary is not in the banner's enumeration and carries no marker for this clause, while the same file's own Out of Scope row - amended by this diff - says the opposite. Against them, :40 reads "The page is designed as a generic \"Requests\" page — currently only vacation, but structured to accommodate future request types." The `**Amended:**` paragraph at :42-44 sits directly beneath it and corrects only the role gate and the default filter; it says nothing about request types. The banner at :26 claims "Every statement this overrules is marked in place, each beside the text it corrects" and its enumeration at :27-33 does not name the Summary. The shipped page draws three types: STATUS/TYPE options in apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx and parseRequestTypeQuery in packages/validation/src/requests.ts.

findings.rule: none - judgement (state written but never read)
findings.claim: Three residues in the resume path. (a) `run.resumes` is written here and read nowhere - cmdStatus does not print it and scripts/run-report.mjs does not open it - so the comment's promise that a run reaching `ready` still shows who overruled what holds only for someone opening run.json by hand. (b) The reset loop deletes endedAt and sets status='pending' for stages at and after the resume point but leaves startedAt and lastVerdict, so `wf status` shows a pending stage carrying the verdict of a pass that was discarded. (c) The new stage-closing loop covers STAGES.slice(0, indexOf(stage)) only, so the most common abandoned-run case - the killed stage is itself the resume target - gets no stage-end event, and the board keeps that attempt growing.

witness.detail: The orchestrator dies mid-implement; `wf resume --stage implement` writes no stage-end for implement, because slice(0,2) covers preflight and pre_implement only. `npm run board` then shows the killed attempt still counting upward toward Date.now(). Separately `wf status` prints a pending stage alongside the lastVerdict of the pass the resume threw away.

findings.suggestedFix: Close a running stage at the resume point too, delete lastVerdict and startedAt along with endedAt in the reset loop, and surface `resumes` in cmdStatus so the record is read by something.
